feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the experience. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and could be sharper by reducing overlap, tightening phrasing, and adding more outcome-focused metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Strong scope and relevance: web modernization, analytics, governance, email, social, and multimedia are all well aligned to the target title.  
- Generally high writing quality: professional tone, strong verbs, and no obvious misspellings; formatting is mostly consistent.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more measurable impact: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include outcomes such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or campaign impact.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (e.g., “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); consider consistent punctuation/hyphenation in bullets and section labels.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and relevant scope. It reads well, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and fix style: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience.”
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: enterprise web modernization, cross-channel leadership, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Add clearer positioning tied to recent roles, e.g., digital strategy, governance, analytics, and platform transformation.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, editorial workflows, and digital governance. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused content and coordinating stakeholders across complex organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflows and systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is supported in experience, but avoid overloading the intro with terms already emphasized elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the competencies more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, noun-based phrasing and tighten wording: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications • CMS & web operations • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow automation & systems design • Advocacy & policy communications • Stakeholder coordination • Multimedia & live event production
- Replace “multi-channel communication” with “cross-channel communications” for more natural, standard CV language.
- Consider swapping “Web & CMS administration” for “CMS & web operations” to sound more strategic and current.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve more technical terms here for differentiation, e.g., “workflow automation” instead of repeating generic “workflow.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Header and Soft Skills.
- “Digital strategy,” “analytics,” “multimedia,” and “advocacy communication” are already reinforced in Topline Skills and Work Experience.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics to improve cross-team coordination, publishing efficiency, and performance visibility.”
- Consolidate web build details into one line: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsites, and member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- End with the most distinctive/current work: “Leading an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in the 2022–2024 director role.
- Specific microsite/search examples may be better left to Recent Projects unless you add measurable results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale metrics; it should read more like an executive achievement entry and less like a responsibility summary. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and business outcomes while trimming overlap with adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening summary with an outcome-led line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and front-load the biggest wins: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: email/social growth, reporting efficiency, production cost/time savings from the studio, or governance improvements such as faster publishing or fewer workflow bottlenecks.
- Consider a sharper sequence: website modernization → channel leadership → analytics stack expansion → in-house studio build → governance/operations improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior Associate Communications Director role; focus here on scale, strategy, and performance improvements.
- Video/programming language overlaps with older NACo entries and Recent Projects; stress building the studio and expanding organizational capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with both the more senior Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around scope, channel ownership, and systems/process impact at this career stage.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial and advocacy output.”
- Combine and streamline bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Recast process bullets to show cross-functional leadership: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullets.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this item as scaling/formalizing the program rather than originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and emphasize higher-value leadership themes rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive terms:  
- Enterprise digital strategy  
- Content governance & editorial operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector advocacy communications  
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “editorial planning” if you want stronger alignment with your recent leadership roles.
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise web strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Keep wording parallel and noun-based; avoid mixing broad strategy terms with softer execution language.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” overlap heavily with the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is weaker than the repeated “communications” framing used elsewhere; “advocacy communications” would align better.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills line, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript)”
- Group related items for readability: “CMS modernization and migration • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems”
- Keep the most distinctive, recent strength last: “AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

Possible rewrite:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the technical section carry the full tool list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider using “search and discovery” here to reduce repetition.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and undersells strategic value. In Topline Skills, emphasize decision-making and optimization outcomes over repeating software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger business language such as “Executive dashboards and performance reporting.”
- Tighten to something like: “Analytics strategy • KPI design • Executive dashboards • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; Topline Skills should stay higher-level and more strategic.
- “SEO and performance analysis” overlaps with the broader analytics theme; consider “performance optimization” for cleaner phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it more specific to senior-level delivery and systems ownership, not just production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability statement: “Broadcast-quality video and hybrid event production • Livestream operations • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event delivery”
- Consider adding leadership/ownership language: “Studio build-out and operations” or “End-to-end multimedia production”
- If accurate, add scale or complexity: “Hybrid and virtual event production for advocacy programming and member-facing events”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing verbs and nouns (“Video production and editing” vs “Livestreaming”)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially duplicates Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”
- “Studio operations” and event production are already evidenced in the 2022–2024 Director role, so avoid overloading this section with the same phrasing

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or removed to reduce repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize platforms tied to recent work and depth of use: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages”
- Drop “GitHub Pages” unless you’ve used it meaningfully in recent roles; it feels lightweight beside enterprise CMS platforms.
- If space allows, add proficiency cues instead of just listing names, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; if this section stays, consider renaming to “CMS Platforms” for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical capabilities.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles, so repeating it here without context adds little.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should be tighter, more implementation-focused, and emphasize current/recent tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioning (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more current.
- Move jQuery to the end or remove it if not central to recent work; it can signal older experience unless framed as legacy support.
- If space allows, add scope/context instead of more tools, e.g., “front-end implementation, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider keeping this section tool-specific and letting Topline Skills carry the broader “technical execution” language.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems**.
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier** | **Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello** | **Slack, Microsoft Teams**.
- If accurate, add light qualifiers to show depth, not just exposure: e.g. **Airtable (system design), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (project workflow management)**.
- Consider trimming older/basic collaboration tools if space is tight and prioritizing the most relevant recent systems tied to current work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Slack/Teams may be too generic unless other technical lists are equally tool-specific.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this line should stay concise and emphasize platform breadth rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS match: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier instead of just listing tools, e.g. **campaign automation, newsletter distribution, audience engagement**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was minimal or older, remove it

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” or “email strategy” here; those are already covered in recent NACo roles
- Don’t repeat workflow/automation language already captured under **Automation & Workflow Systems** unless it is email-specific

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership: “Supported a major website refresh, coordinating digital content updates and production needs across channels.”
- Tighten production language: “Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates that expanded the organization’s in-house multimedia output.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, website traffic impact, or team size/associate supervised.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; distinguish this role as launching/building the format rather than scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo roles; keep this version focused on foundational setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, initiative, and any concrete output or audience value.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout contribution: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; partnered across teams to turn findings into member-facing content and communications materials.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more outcome-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specific deliverables if known: web articles, multimedia packages, interviews, briefing materials, or campaign assets.
- If possible, add 1 metric: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders engaged, or programs/policy teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership here; save team-building and enterprise digital impact for the more recent director/associate roles.
